criteria.evidence: The opened asset is the expected Sigma Pi collection; raw Purdue GIS feature FID 776 names Sigma Pi (SOSP) at 130 Russell St. The official Sigma Pi location page and Purdue Off-Campus Housing listing independently identify 130 N Russell. The exported shell bottom was directly compared to all 36 unique GIS vertices; maximum nearest error is 0.000017 m. Current state orthophoto overlay corroborates the GIS ring as roof-plan perimeter.
criteria.uncertainty: GIS and orthophoto identify the roof outline; the exterior structural wall line and eave offset are not surveyed.

criteria.evidence: Direct inspection of the loaded mesh gives shell world bounds [[-439.1611328125, -419.6351013183594], [-179.7059326171875, -146.538818359375], [0.25, 9.350000381469727]]; the 36-vertex source ring is reconstructed with max XY error 0.000017 m. Source ring projection reconciles GIS planar EPSG:3857 area/length with the layer values within rounding, and the overlay matches current orthophoto.
criteria.uncertainty: Plan location and roof perimeter are strong; no surveyed structural wall line or height control is available.

criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.evidence: The actual saved asset contains a separate triangulated roof mesh with 1436 vertices and 2708 faces, world bounds [[-439.1572570800781, -419.6893005371094], [-179.653076171875, -146.5334014892578], [9.486756324768066, 12.568769454956055]], and 0 nonmanifold edges. The 2018 LiDAR source records 1,094 filtered unclassified surface returns, with percentile roof heights around 9.74–12.25 m above local ground; the mesh follows a varied surface rather than a flat cap.
criteria.uncertainty: The LiDAR returns are class 1 and may include vegetation; no class-6 returns were available. Shell height/story count remain estimates and GIS NUM_LEVELS conflicts with chapter multi-deck clues. Neither current roof structure nor present floor count is measured.

criteria.evidence: The loaded asset has 159 named window objects and 3 named entry/door objects. Its R5 preview directly shows masonry base, Tudor-style timber framing and braces, divided street-facing windows, and a modeled entry. These cues closely match the preserved dated November 2004 house photographs on Eta Data pp. 1 and 6; image and PDF hashes match the R5 freeze record.
criteria.uncertainty: The photographs support qualitative as-of-2004 façade cues, not exact dimensions or 2026 condition. Framing is simplified, not all building elevations receive the same detailing, and the gabled roof silhouette visible in the photos is not modeled as gables.

criteria.criterion: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
criteria.evidence: The SHA-256 matches the frozen target exactly and the file opened without errors in bpy 4.5.15 LTS; the loaded asset contains 266 collection objects (266 meshes), 0 shell nonmanifold edges, 0 linked libraries, 0 unpacked external images, and 0 unpacked image textures. 15/15 expected key source/evidence files are present. Frozen R5 preview and both dated November 2004 photo crops match their registered SHA-256 values.
criteria.uncertainty: The available inspector is Blender Python 4.5.15, not the builder's Blender 5.2.3; Blender warned that it was reading a newer 5.2 file and removed some UI region data. Mesh geometry was inspected read-only, but a matching 5.2.3 runtime was unavailable. Coordinator manifest reconciliation and master integration remain pending.

findings: Identity and exact GIS roof-plan registration are strongly supported by official chapter location, GIS feature, raw geometry, and current aerial overlay.

The revised asset includes an articulated LiDAR-derived roof surface; this is a clear improvement over the prior flat roof cap, but class-1 returns do not prove roof-only surfaces and the wall height/story count remain estimated.

The dated 2004 chapter-house photos are now preserved with page-level crops and match the R5 freeze hashes. The R5 preview models the distinctive timber framing, divided windows, brick base and entry; framing remains simplified and the historic multi-gabled roof form is not represented.
The file opened read-only in bpy 4.5.15 and mesh geometry was inspected directly, but an exact-version Blender 5.2.3 independent reopen was unavailable. No asset data was saved or changed.

Height and floor count remain the largest evidence gaps: the roof uses unclassified LiDAR returns and its interpolated surface does not represent the dated photographs' explicit gabled roof silhouette.
